segments.narration_text: The feedback pile is growing again. One note says, “I could not tell where to start.” Another asks for a reminder. A third says the task looked complete but the page gave no confirmation. These are fictional member comments carried forward from our earlier exercise. If we group them too quickly under “improve onboarding,” we lose the difference between finding an action, remembering it, and knowing it worked.

segments.narration_text: The simulation points to two questions, not two answers. First: can an eligible new member explain the first action before beginning it? Second: after acting, can they tell whether it worked? Put each beside a real observation method. The research owner can watch an approved session, ask the person what they expect, and record the observed hesitation.

segments.narration_text: The structure helps you see where a source ends and an inference begins. It also helps you avoid asking a model to settle a question only people can answer. The next module uses this discipline to examine strategic shifts and future concepts. Bring the job and the unresolved question forward. If the evidence is weak, say so.
